mof_ops.detail: MoF May 2026 supply: three regular sale auctions - 13 May (settle 15 May) PLN 6,000-12,000m, 21 May (settle 25 May) 7,000-13,000m, 27 May (settle 29 May) 6,000-12,000m, each in OK0129 / NZ0331 / PS0731 / DS0436 / NZ0936 'plus possible IZ and other series' (total 19-37bn); final offer 2 days before each auction; additional sale after each auction at the minimum accepted price. NO switch auctions planned in May. One T-bill auction: 8 May (settle 12 May), 46-week bills maturing 30 Mar 2027, PLN 3,000-6,000m. OK0129 replaces OK0128 as the 2Y zero (first offered in this plan; DB shows first sale 13 May). Retail offer for May: OTS0826 2.00%, ROR0527 4.00% (ref+0.00), DOR0528 4.15% (ref+0.15), TOS0529 4.40%, COI0530 4.75% (CPI+1.50), EDO0536 5.35% (CPI+2.00), ROS0532 5.00%, ROD0538 5.60% (first periods). Deputy FM Jurand Drop (comment to the plan, PAP Skrot 17:02): budget accounts ~PLN 184bn at end-April. PKO's Budzicki (PAP 17:03): the 19-37bn of regular sales compares with his expectation of two regular plus one switch auction totalling ~29bn - may cap any bond rebound.

mof_ops.detail: No switch or buyback in the windows. The May plan (30 Apr) states 'Przetargi zamiany obligacji skarbowych nie sa planowane'. The MoF DB shows no wholesale bond operation dated 29 Apr-12 May; the only bond operation in the windows is the 13 May sale.

Financing of 2026 gross borrowing needs (budget act): ~49% at end-April (PAP weekly preview 11 May 06:16; same figure MoF gave after the 28 Apr sale). No newer ratio after the 8 May bills or the 13 May sale found in the windows. April regular sales incl. additional = 30.35bn (April facts). May regular supply plan 19-37bn; 13 May delivered 11.85bn incl. additional. Budget accounts ~PLN 184bn at end-April (Drop, 30 Apr). Budget execution after April NOT published in the windows (MoF publishes around the 15th; last known: deficit 69.56bn after March).

Retail bond sales April 2026 PLN 5,609.1m (March 7,274.0m); ROR 2,216.2m (40%), COI 1,064.1m (19%), TOS 17%, EDO 13%, DOR 6%, OTS 3%; YTD 24,769.4m (MoF communique, PAP 8 May 10:12). May retail coupons in the 30 Apr plan (see monthly_plan).

MoF: non-resident holdings of domestic SPW fell PLN 5.0bn in March to 190.0bn (share 12.2% from 12.7% in Feb; 11.8% end-2025). Domestic SPW debt +11.4bn to 1,551.0bn; banks incl. NBP +12.3bn to 806.0bn (52.0%), domestic non-banks +4.1bn to 555.1bn (35.8%) (PAP 15:13). SPW secondary-market turnover in March +37.5% m/m to PLN 2,430.8bn (Skrot 17:02).

MoF: EU funds inflow in March EUR 3.956bn (cohesion 3.235bn, CAP 0.539bn), YTD 9.269bn; Poland paid in 540.9m in March, YTD 2.363bn (PAP 13:06). BGK: EU 2021-27 payouts ~PLN 76.05bn by 8 May (Skrot 11 May 17:02).

No foreign bond issue, mandate or FX-account communique in the windows. The MoF 'komunikaty-dlug' list shows nothing between the 30 Apr May plan and two 15 May notices (April FX account; 2025 market transactions) - both outside, titles only seen, not used. The USD 6bn issue of 7 Apr is pre-window.

facts.text: PKO Dziennik 30 Apr: on 29 Apr POLGB yields rose 4-6bp as Brent topped $120 and the Fed held with hawkish dissents; April ESI 100.2; PKO expects April CPI at 3.0% with no market impact absent a surprise; FX range 4.2550-4.27 EUR/PLN.

WIIW cut Poland's GDP forecast to 3.6% (2026) from 3.7% and 2.6% (2027) from 3.2%; CPI 3.5% (2026) and 3.7% (2027) vs 3.0/2.7 in January; GG deficit 6.5% (2026) and 6.2% (2027); balance of risks: lower growth, higher inflation; fiscal policy to stay expansionary.
PAP FX/FI morning: PAP consensus for April flash CPI 3.0% y/y, 0.4% m/m; Erste 3.0%; Millennium: oil at ~$122 and core-market selling may lift POLGB yields with limited impact from domestic CPI.

GUS flash CPI April 2026: 3.2% y/y, 0.6% m/m (PAP consensus 3.0% / 0.4%; March 3.0% / 1.1%). Food 1.9% y/y (0.6% m/m), energy 4.7% (0.5% m/m), fuels 8.4% y/y (-1.8% m/m after +15.4% in March). Full data on 15 May.

Economists on April CPI: ING - no May hike but core ~2.9% means sharper MPC rhetoric; food and energy above expectations, fuel fell thanks to CPN. Bank Pocztowy (Kurtek): core 2.9-3.0%; if the war lasts CPI will soon breach the 3.5% upper band - forget further cuts, higher odds of hikes.

NBP Quick Monitoring (Q1 2026): firms' 12M CPI expectations jumped (balance 46.4 vs 29.3, long-run mean 32.6; share expecting higher CPI 43.6% vs 25.3%, 51.1% after 28 Feb); larger planned price rises in Q2 (input costs); fewer firms plan wage rises within a year; labour demand to weaken further in Q2; slight improvement in Q2 outlook.
MoF: EU funds inflow March EUR 3.956bn (cohesion 3.235bn, CAP 0.539bn); YTD 9.269bn.
MoF: non-residents cut domestic SPW holdings by PLN 5.0bn in March to 190.0bn (share 12.2% from 12.7%); banks incl. NBP +12.3bn to 806.0bn; total domestic SPW debt 1,551.0bn (+11.4bn).

MoF May supply plan: sales 13 May (6-12bn), 21 May (7-13bn), 27 May (6-12bn) in OK0129/NZ0331/PS0731/DS0436/NZ0936 (+possible IZ/other); no switch; 46-week T-bill 8 May 3-6bn. Drop: budget accounts ~PLN 184bn at end-April. SPW secondary turnover March +37.5% m/m to 2,430.8bn.
facts.time_basis: gov.pl page date 30 Apr; PAP Skrot 17:02 = upper bound

facts.text: MPC's Ireneusz Dabrowski (Bloomberg, cited by PAP): chances of rate cuts in Poland fell significantly after April's CPI acceleration.

Pekao: a prolonged fuel crisis is becoming the base case; second-round effects must be taken seriously; CPI may exceed 4% y/y at end-2026; no rate changes this year, shifting toward considering hikes.

Poland told the European Commission the temporary fuel VAT cut aims to curb war-driven prices (source close to diplomacy; EC analysing). Defence minister Kosiniak-Kamysz: Poland ready to sign the SAFE loan agreement next week, ~PLN 20bn advance after signing.

PAP FX/FI close (PKO Budzicki): POLGB yields back near the late-March local highs on geopolitics, the CPI beat and oil; the market starts to price extreme scenarios incl. a full 75bp of NBP hikes within 12M; any positive news could take 2Y to at least 4.5% and 10Y to 5.7%; the bigger-than-expected May supply (19-37bn vs his 29bn) could cap a rebound; EUR/PLN 4.2558.
Millennium daily 30 Apr: BGK sold FPC0229/0231/0332/0235 for 694m on 940m demand on 29 Apr and a further 129.5m at the additional sale; 10Y POLGB ~5.80% at the 29 Apr close (+3-4bp).

1-3 May (Skrot 3 May): SAFE plenipotentiary Sobkowiak-Czarnecka (Sat): the government will sign the SAFE loan agreement with the EC within hours/days and receive a 15% advance; Kosiniak-Kamysz: signing on Friday if all goes well. Trump announced 25% tariffs on EU cars (Sikorski: bad news for Poland's auto-parts sector).

PAP weekly preview: MPC decision Wed 6 May (no change expected; ECB June-hike signal and the CPI beat are hawkish inputs); Goldman Sachs: NBP on hold until Q1 2027; ING: hold but a more hawkish tone; Millennium: stable-rate factors include fading labour market and possible CPN extension to at least June. S&P and DBRS review Poland Fri 8 May after 22:00 - Erste sees a sizeable risk of an S&P outlook cut to negative (S&P is the only one of the big three still stable). T-bill 8 May 46-week 3-6bn (14:00 minutes RPP 8 May; MF offer 7 May 15:00).

NBP 2025 annual accounts: loss PLN 35.740bn (2024: 13.347bn) - FX revaluation -36.74bn, monetary-policy result -20.96bn, reserve management +24.69bn; no transfer to the budget. NBP raised ETF holdings to 79.7bn (equity ETFs and USD corporate-bond ETFs).

PKO Dziennik 4 May: April CPI 3.2% was a broad surprise (smaller fuel fall, higher food); CPI may temporarily exceed 3.5% in the next two months but mostly stay within the tolerance band, which justifies stable rates; POLGB curve rose strongly last week on Middle East escalation fears.

Erste Codziennik 4 May: CPI 3.2% vs Erste 3.0% and market 2.9%; core estimated up to 2.9% from 2.7%; CPI to rise further in May and may approach 4% if Brent stays above $100. Erste FRA table (30 Apr close): 1x4 3.86, 3x6 4.05, 6x9 4.37, 9x12 4.57 (WIBOR 3M 3.84).
PAP FX/FI morning: PKO - peace talks without new military action should allow a correction, 2Y yields at least to 4.4% and 10Y to 5.6%; BGK: 4.25 EUR/PLN base case.

NBP senior loan officer survey: banks eased corporate and household credit terms in Q1; for Q2 they plan to tighten criteria for large firms, keep SMEs unchanged and ease for households, expecting higher demand for all loan types.
NBP: Governor Glapinski's post-MPC press conference on Thu 7 May at 15:00 (decision Wed 6 May).

PAP FX/FI (Millennium): the market prices no change at the MPC but NBP hikes in coming months; S&P will publish its review this week but no major change expected; slight further yield rise possible, resistance ~6% on the 10Y.

S&P Global manufacturing PMI April 48.8 (March 48.7; consensus 48.7 per PKO, 48.6 per Millennium); strongest input-cost growth since May 2022, stock-building, new orders down 13th month. Economists: a slight rise but a worrying structure.

Energy minister Motyka (TOK FM): if the CPN fuel package is extended, probably by another two weeks; any end-date declarations are premature. PM Tusk: Poland likely ready to sign SAFE on Friday (~PLN 20bn advance).

PKO Dziennik 5 May: on 4 May POLGB yields rose 3-11bp on renewed Hormuz tension; PMI met expectations; the market already prices a 25bp NBP hike in 2026 plus 50bp in 2027; hawkish MPC tone possible; EC received Poland's SAFE loan agreement; PKO thinks the fuel VAT/excise cuts may last to year-end.

PAP FX/FI morning: ING - 10Y POLGB around 5.78%, near a one-month high; hawkish MPC narrative, solid May supply and the S&P 'fiscal reminder' should keep yields elevated; hike pricing for end-2026/early-2027 is too aggressive but stabilises PLN.
NBP: banking sector net profit Jan-Mar 2026 PLN 9.427bn, -19.6% y/y (March ~3.35bn).
Government adopted the OKI (personal investment account) bill; to take effect from early 2027.

PAP FX/FI close (Bank Pocztowy Kurtek): POLGB yields rose while core yields fell (also in CZ/HU); the debt market awaits a more hawkish Glapinski after the CPI beat and possibly large MoF supply; EUR/PLN 4.2479.

PKO Dziennik 6 May: market pricing is shifting toward stronger tightening; chart: FRAs price the NBP reference rate at least at 4.5% in early 2027. 5 May close per PKO table: PL2Y 4.61 (-6bp), PL5Y 5.50, PL10Y 5.80.
Erste Codziennik 6 May: IRS and FRA rose ahead of the MPC (FRA 6x9 +7bp to 4.43, 9x12 +6bp to 4.62 at the 5 May close).

PAP survey: economists expect the MPC to keep the reference rate at 3.75% on 6 May and through 2026, possibly to end-2027, with a possible 25bp cut in Q4 2027. PKO: Glapinski's comments may show how likely the hikes priced for this year are.
NBP: the June MPC meeting moves to 1-2 June (from 9-10 June); Governor's conference 3 June 15:00; minutes 5 June.
MPC (5-6 May) left all NBP rates unchanged, as expected: reference 3.75%, lombard 4.25%, deposit 3.25%, rediscount 3.80%, discount 3.85%.

MPC statement: April CPI 3.2% (fuels); core inflation probably also rose in April; given that and geopolitical uncertainty rates were kept; risk factors unchanged (commodity prices and global inflation, fiscal policy and fuel-price regulation, activity, wages); Q1 GDP growth probably slowed; NBP may intervene in FX.

Economists on the decision: Millennium - statement unchanged in key parts, wait-and-see, hold at least to July; Kurtek - balance of risks toward hikes; ING (Antoniak) - hold to year-end, July projection the first quantification; PKO - hikes priced by the market will not be needed, reference rate unchanged to year-end.
Kosiniak-Kamysz: the EC is ready to sign the SAFE loan agreement with Poland in Warsaw on Friday 8 May at 13:00.

PAP FX/FI close (ING Sutowicz): on US-Iran deal hopes the market pared hike bets - it had priced 75bp of NBP hikes within 10 months; the 10Y POLGB fell ~20bp; further falls possible on peace news; EUR/PLN 4.2323 (two-week low 4.2260 intraday). Note: the PAP headline/Skrot text says yields 'rose' double digits - contradicted by the body (yields fell).

PKO Dziennik 7 May: POLGB yields fell 17-22bp on 6 May with core markets; the MPC decision was neutral; a US-Iran memorandum could extend the fall. 6 May close: PL2Y 4.45 (-17bp), PL5Y 5.28 (-22bp), PL10Y 5.60 (-20bp). Chart of FRA-implied NBP path (27 Apr vs 6 May).
Erste Codziennik 7 May: 6 May yields -16bp on 2Y, -20-22bp further out; FRA 3x6 -9bp, longer contracts -19-22bp (6x9 4.22, 9x12 4.40).
NBP official reserve assets April EUR 254.77bn (March 253.53bn); monetary gold USD 88.38bn (85.42bn).

Glapinski (conference 15:00): asked whether the probability of a hike has risen since April - 'Tak'; hikes possible ('every member allows a hike or hikes if inflation rises'), a cut very unlikely though not excluded; CPI 3.2% still within target (upper band 3.5%); a breach of the band with forecasts of persistence - or even projections showing an unavoidable breach while CPI is below 3.5% - would prompt immediate action; core is rising (e.g. air fares) but demand is not overheating, wage growth in enterprises is at a five-year low, Q1 GDP likely slowed; rates are high vs the 2022 shock; the March cut was not premature; gold 595t (target 700t), unrealised gold gain ~PLN 160bn.

Reactions: Pekao - a 'hawkish' conference, hike probability rose over the month; ING - NBP more hawkish than in April but still wait-and-see, the July projection is key; PIE - the energy shock limits room for cuts, first signs of spillover beyond energy. Pekao revised up its CPI path: peak near 4% around end-2026 (Q3/Q4 turn).

PAP FX/FI close: PLN barely reacted to Glapinski; bonds benefit less than FX from improved sentiment (PKO Adamiak: inflation worries keep bonds from recovering; the market removed 2026 cuts; PKO still hopes for cuts in 2027). XTB: FRAs price ~2 NBP hikes by year-end vs slightly over 3 at the start of the week; Glapinski sets a high bar for hikes. EUR/PLN 4.2265.
MoF: the 8 May T-bill auction offers 46-week bills for PLN 3-6bn.
facts.time_basis: MoF slot 15:00; PAP Skrot 17:06 = upper bound

facts.text: FM Domanski: the Middle East conflict has so far had little impact on Poland's economy; Poland supports joint EU borrowing for defence.

PKO Dziennik 8 May: despite Glapinski's hawkish message POLGB yields fell slightly on 7 May as hikes were already priced; 7 May close PL2Y 4.40 (-4bp), PL5Y 5.26, PL10Y 5.59; Glapinski's conditions: CPI above the band with persistent forecasts, or forecasts alone with CPI below 3.5%.

Millennium daily 8 May: the conference was hawkish but does not imply quick hikes - wait-and-see, July projection key; Millennium keeps stable rates to year-end; S&P decision after the close, no rating/outlook change expected (ratings likely unchanged until the 2027 election).
MPC's Kotecki (TOK FM): all forecasts seen in the last two days indicate inflation will stay within the target.
MoF: retail bond sales April PLN 5,609.1m (March 7,274.0m); ROR 40%, COI 19%; YTD 24,769.4m.
MRPiPS flash: registered unemployment April 6.0% (March 6.1%; PAP consensus 6.0%); 935.8k unemployed, +133.1k y/y; Labour Fund cuts limit activation programmes.

April MPC minutes (8-9 Apr meeting): most members said the war-driven supply shock lifts CPI short term but hurts activity, which - if lasting - may weaken demand and curb medium-term inflation; holding rates was justified; the inflation outlook is uncertain even short term; some members pointed to the high public deficit in the context of fuel measures; some noted higher short-term consumer inflation expectations in March; the shock is smaller than in 2022 (gas, coal, agri prices, supply chains), demand and wages weaker, rates higher; 2026 GDP may undershoot earlier forecasts if energy prices stay high.

Poland signed the SAFE loan agreement with the EC (up to EUR 43.7bn of low-cost defence loans; Tusk: a breakthrough). Domanski: savings for public finances may reach PLN 80bn. Kosiniak-Kamysz ready to bring the PSL 'SAFE 0%' bill to the cabinet.

PKO BP (Skrot): the risk of an MPC hike has risen markedly; if Hormuz is not unblocked a hike could come as early as July. Erste's Bielski: every week of conflict raises the risk of worse public finances; MoF's planned consolidation is symbolic even in its optimistic scenario.

PAP FX/FI weekly close (PKO Kiedrowicz): POLGB yields fell by double digits (more than 10bp) on the week; Friday -2-3bp on lower core yields and Brent attempts below $100; a US-Iran memorandum could push yields toward the April lows or lower; PLN +0.36% vs EUR on the week (EUR/PLN ~4.23).

S&P Global Ratings affirmed Poland at A-/A-2 (foreign currency) and A/A-1 (local currency), outlook STABLE (first review since the Middle East war; markets had feared an outlook cut like Fitch's and Moody's). S&P: stable outlook balances promising two-year growth prospects against rising vulnerability from fast debt growth; GDP 3.3% (2026) / 2.9% (2027); GG deficit 7.3% of GDP in 2025, staying high; net debt approaching 70% of GDP by 2029; political polarisation and the 2027 election hamper fiscal and institutional policy, no significant consolidation expected before the election. Downgrade if medium-term growth weakens markedly or the Russia-Ukraine war escalates; upgrade if large deficits are cut and debt stabilises.

facts.text: FM Domanski (X) on the S&P affirmation: confirmation of the economy's resilience despite geopolitical tension, higher oil and weaker Europe. MoF communique (EN) dated 10 May repeats S&P's rationale.

facts.text: Energy minister Motyka (Sun): the ministry recommends keeping the 'Ceny Paliwa Nizej' programme (valid to 15 May); decision early next week.

PAP weekly preview: Q1 GDP flash Thu 14 May (Erste 3.8%, PKO 3.4%, PAP April consensus 3.5%; Q4 4.1%); April CPI details and March C/A Fri 15 May (Erste C/A -1.8bn EUR vs market -1.3bn; Erste: core accelerated to 2.9%); MoF sale Wed 13 May (details Mon 15:00), BGK FPC tender Thu 14 May (details Tue 15:00); ~49% of 2026 gross borrowing needs financed at end-April; budget data after April due around the 15th (after March deficit 69.5bn); Scope review Fri 15 May.

PKO Dziennik 11 May: S&P affirmed A-/stable (markets had feared a negative outlook); POLGB falls may be limited by the hawkish MPC and the 13 May auction (6-12bn per plan); later in Q2 PKO expects the curve to fall a further 10-20bp; near term sideways.

Millennium daily 11 May: MoF sold PLN 3.66bn of 46-week T-bills on 8 May at demand 3.66bn and a 4.151% yield (offer 3-6bn). Millennium also: S&P affirmation closes the spring rating round; seasonally adjusted unemployment 6.0% vs 5.9%.

PAP morning: Morningstar DBRS confirmed Poland's long-term foreign-currency rating at 'A' with a NEGATIVE trend (trend already negative since Nov 2025). The review was scheduled for Fri 8 May after 22:00 (PAP calendar); exact DBRS release time not retrieved - put here strictly by first dated mention.

facts.text: PAP FX/FI morning: Trump rejected Iran's reply as 'totally unacceptable'; Erste expects weaker PLN and higher yields; Millennium: debt may lose ahead of the MoF and BGK auctions; PKO sideways near term.
GUS: average gross wage in the national economy Q1 2026 PLN 9,562.88, +6.7% y/y (Q4 2025 8.5%; NBP March projection 7.1% per Erste), +3.97% q/q; real ~+4.3% (PKO).

PAP FX/FI (Millennium): yields fell last week on oil but the 'not dovish' Glapinski lifted rates in the second half of the week, continuing Monday; oil toward $105, MoF/BGK auctions and solid GDP data may push yields up; nearest 10Y resistance ~5.75%.
ING: Q1 GDP growth slightly below Q4 2025; further slowdown expected in Q2.
President signed the amendment allowing ARP loans to JSW and Grupa Azoty (JSW plans an 850m ARP loan).

PKO Dziennik 12 May: MPC's Wnorowski said there is no need to hike now despite higher inflation as policy is restrictive enough, but the MPC has turned more hawkish and the risk of hikes has risen; exceeding the 3.5% upper band could sharpen the debate; base case still wait-and-see; GDP growth now closer to 3% vs 4%+ expected earlier. (Original interview/source not identified.) 11 May close: PL2Y 4.50 (+6bp), PL5Y 5.39 (+11), PL10Y 5.70 (+10); S&P's stable outlook supported PLN.

facts.text: Erste Codziennik 12 May: Q1 wage growth 6.7% in line with Erste, below the NBP projection; Motyka (11 May): VAT/excise extension decision probably by Wednesday, two more weeks if markets stay tense; 11 May POLGB yields +5-11bp, curve steeper ~6bp; IRS +7-8bp, FRA +0-12bp (9x12 4.56).

Energy minister Motyka: the CPN programme (to 15 May) will be extended by two weeks 'within hours' via MoF regulations; VAT on fuel 8% (from 23%) and excise cut 29gr/l petrol, 28gr/l diesel; statutory basis for excise cuts runs to 30 June.
PAP FX/FI morning: BGK expects DS1035 at 5.65-5.70% and the new 10Y benchmark DS0436 at 5.75-5.80%; limited room for POLGBs to recover given US CPI and Iran; ING: GDP flash Thu, CPI and BoP Fri.

MPC's Zarzecki (PAP Biznes interview): 'the time for cuts has passed'; base case is a pause through end-2026, but the probability of a hike has clearly risen; hikes would be considered only if current CPI exceeds 3.5% AND projections keep it above 3.5% in the medium/long term; also watching pass-through to core and de-anchoring of expectations; the May meeting discussed conditions for such scenarios; persistent fiscal expansion justifies moderately restrictive policy; strong PLN allows a rate gap vs the ECB; awaits the July projection; 'signalling' hikes would be dangerous.

Fiscal Council opinion on the MoF's 2026-30 macro assumptions (WZM): the shock scenario is relatively optimistic on the size and duration of the energy-price shock; an understated inflation path may imply an over-optimistic interest-rate path.
Pekao cut its GDP forecasts to 3.5% (2026) from 3.8% and 2.7% (2027) from 3.6% on the prolonged Gulf conflict and weak consumption and exports. IERiGZ: food prices to rise 2-2.5%.
BGK offers FPC0229, FPC0231, FPC0332 and FPC0235 at the 14 May FPC tender, minimum PLN 500m.
facts.time_basis: BGK slot 15:00; PAP Skrot 17:02 = upper bound

facts.text: PKO Dziennik 13 May: POLGB yields rose 3-8bp on 12 May with oil and US CPI; Polish bonds behave relatively well vs core markets - the long end is supported by last week's favourable S&P report and more hawkish MPC rhetoric; Zarzecki's base case of no change to end-2026.

Erste Codziennik 13 May: NBP data - Q1 housing transaction prices in the 7 largest cities -0.3% y/y primary, -0.7% secondary; Fiscal Council criticised WZM inflation assumptions (government 2.5% average 2026 CPI; Erste: very likely above 3%); FRA up >9bp for 9M+ contracts on 12 May (9x12 4.66).

PAP FX/FI morning: focus on the first May MoF sale (6-11bn of OK0129, PS0130, NZ0331, PS0731, DS0436, NZ0936); 30Y UST above 5%, 30Y Bund 3.63%, 30Y gilt 5.80%; PKO: POLGBs relatively resilient vs core markets.
IPAG: GDP 3.4% (2026), 2.9% (2027); Q1 3.7%; CPI average 3.0% (2026), 2.7% (2027); price pressure at least to end-Q3.

MPC's Litwiniuk (Impact'26): by end-2026 a hike is more likely than a cut; no further cuts given geopolitical uncertainty; the MPC is ready to hike if expectations de-anchor or wage-price risks grow; but he does not expect decisions in July - the July projection opens a period of reflection; almost nobody on the MPC backs a hike scenario yet.

MoF: reduced fuel VAT (8%) and excise cuts extended to 31 May 2026 (regulations published in Dz.U. on 13 May). Domanski: CPN extended to end-May. Motyka: statutory basis guaranteed to end-June, June decisions on extending it; a windfall-profits tax bill may soon go to the Sejm.
MoF sold OK0129, PS0130, NZ0331, PS0731 and DS0436 for PLN 11,006.33m on demand of 13,727.33m (offer 6-11bn); additional sale OK0129 848m. POLGB yields +6bp vs the morning; EUR/PLN 4.25.

MPC's Kotecki (PAP Biznes): forget rate cuts even until mid-2027; stable rates are now more likely, but if the Middle East conflict and its consequences persist, a discussion of hikes could start from July.

Domanski (Impact'26): windfall-tax details ready within seven days; MoF will work on the 3% digital tax (cabinet plan Q3). IMF's Georgieva: Poland's macro stability requires a smaller fiscal deficit; adjustment should not be delayed too long.
PIE Monthly Business Index (MIK) May 94.5, -9.1pt m/m, declines in all sectors. Eurostat: Polish industrial output March +5.3% y/y (wda); employment Q1 +1.3% y/y, +0.2% q/q.

digest.2026-05-04: 30 Apr: April flash CPI rose to 3.2% y/y (0.6% m/m) vs 3.0% expected; core seen near 2.9-3.0% and Dabrowski said cut chances fell sharply. MoF's May plan: sales 13, 21 and 27 May (PLN 6-12bn, 7-13bn, 6-12bn) with a new 2Y OK0129, a 46-week T-bill on 8 May (3-6bn), no switch; budget accounts ~184bn at end-April (Drop). Non-residents cut POLGBs by 5.0bn in March (12.2%). POLGB yields returned to late-March highs; PKO: up to 75bp of NBP hikes priced in 12M. The 30 Apr GPWB change put PS0731 into TBSP. SAFE loan to be signed next week.
digest.2026-05-05: 4 May: manufacturing PMI edged up to 48.8 (48.6-48.7 expected) with the sharpest input-cost rise since 2022; the NBP booked a 2025 loss of PLN 35.7bn; banks plan tighter corporate credit in Q2. Motyka: a CPN fuel-package extension would likely be for two weeks; Tusk: SAFE to be signed Friday. Week ahead: MPC 6 May (hold expected; Glapinski 7 May 15:00), T-bills 8 May, S&P and DBRS after 22:00 on 8 May (Erste sees a sizeable risk of a negative S&P outlook). PKO: peace talks could take 2Y to 4.4% and 10Y to 5.6%; Millennium sees 10Y resistance near 6%.
digest.2026-05-06: 5 May: the MPC began its two-day meeting; POLGB yields edged up (10Y ~5.78%, near a one-month high, ING) as investors braced for a hawkish Glapinski and heavy May supply, after a 3-11bp rise on 4 May (PKO). PKO: the market prices a 25bp NBP hike in 2026 and another 50bp in 2027; ING calls hike pricing too aggressive. The EC received Poland's SAFE loan agreement. Bank-sector Q1 net profit fell 19.6% y/y to PLN 9.4bn. The government adopted the OKI investment-account bill.
digest.2026-05-07: 6 May: the MPC held (ref 3.75%) as expected; the statement says core probably rose in April and keeps wait-and-see amid geopolitical uncertainty; the June meeting moves to 1-2 June. PAP survey: hold through 2026, maybe a cut in Q4 2027; PKO and ING see no hike this year. The 10Y POLGB fell ~20bp on US-Iran deal hopes as the market pared hike bets after pricing 75bp within 10 months (ING); PKO: FRAs price the reference rate at 4.5%+ in early 2027. The EC is ready to sign SAFE on 8 May.
digest.2026-05-08: 7 May: Glapinski: the probability of a hike has risen since April and a cut is very unlikely; a CPI breach of the 3.5% band with forecasts of persistence, or projections making it unavoidable, would trigger action; core is rising but demand and wages are subdued. Pekao called it hawkish, ING still wait-and-see; XTB: FRAs price ~2 hikes by year-end vs >3 early in the week. MoF offers PLN 3-6bn of 46-week bills on 8 May. NBP reserves EUR 254.8bn. Pekao sees CPI near 4% at end-2026. Bonds lagged the PLN rally (PKO).
digest.2026-05-11: 8-10 May: S&P affirmed Poland at A-/stable late on 8 May (no consolidation seen before the 2027 election; Domanski: proof of resilience). April MPC minutes: the war lifts CPI near term but weaker activity may curb medium-term pressure; some flagged the high deficit. Kotecki: forecasts keep CPI within target. PKO: hike risk up markedly, possibly July if Hormuz stays shut. Poland signed the SAFE loan (Domanski: up to PLN 80bn savings). Unemployment 6.0%; retail bonds 5.6bn in April. POLGB yields fell by double digits on the week. ME recommends extending CPN.
digest.2026-05-12: 11 May: Trump rejected Iran's reply and POLGB yields kept rising (Millennium; 10Y resistance ~5.75%) ahead of MoF and BGK supply. Millennium: MoF sold PLN 3.66bn of 46-week bills at 4.151% on 8 May. DBRS kept Poland at A with a negative trend. ~49% of 2026 borrowing needs were financed at end-April. Q1 wages rose 6.7% y/y (8.5% in Q4), below the NBP projection. Week ahead: Q1 GDP flash 14 May (Erste 3.8%, PKO 3.4%), CPI final and C/A 15 May. PKO sees a further 10-20bp fall in yields later in Q2.
digest.2026-05-13: 12 May: MoF offers PLN 6-11bn on 13 May (new 2Y OK0129, PS0130, NZ0331, PS0731, DS0436, NZ0936); BGK offers FPC bonds on 14 May (min 0.5bn). Zarzecki: base case no change through 2026 but hike odds rose; hikes need current and projected CPI above 3.5%. Wnorowski: no need to hike now, though risk has risen. The Fiscal Council called the MoF's shock scenario too optimistic. Motyka: CPN to be extended two weeks. Pekao cut 2026 GDP to 3.5%. Yields rose 6-11bp on 11 May (PKO); BGK sees DS0436 at 5.75-5.80%.
digest.2026-05-14: 13 May: MoF sold PLN 11.0bn (offer 6-11bn, demand 13.7bn, cover 1.25) plus 0.85bn of OK0129 additional - new 2Y OK0129 1.16bn at 4.87%, PS0731 4.02bn at 5.36%, NZ0331 2.43bn, DS0436 2.11bn at 5.85%, PS0130 1.3bn at 5.02%; NZ0936 drew no bids. Litwiniuk: a hike is more likely than a cut by end-2026, but no move in July; Kotecki: forget cuts until mid-2027, hike talk possible from July. Fuel VAT/excise cuts extended to 31 May; windfall-tax details within seven days (Domanski). Yields +6bp on the day.

mpc.gist: Chances of rate cuts fell significantly after the April CPI acceleration.

Hold: ref 3.75, lombard 4.25, deposit 3.25, rediscount 3.80, discount 3.85. Core likely rose in April; wait-and-see on geopolitical uncertainty; risk-factor wording unchanged; FX intervention possible. June meeting moved to 1-2 June (13:27).

Probability of a hike up since April; cut very unlikely; hike if CPI breaches 3.5% with persistent forecasts, or if projections show an unavoidable breach; core rising but demand/wages subdued; rates already high; gold 595t, ~160bn unrealised gain.
Forecasts of the last two days show inflation staying within target.
Majority: war shock raises CPI short term but weakens activity, may curb medium-term pressure; hold justified; some flagged the high deficit; some noted higher consumer inflation expectations.
